elbow-lever-2.png: Entry: hands face backward and stay planted while straight legs extend behind, toes still touching the floor.
one-leg-planche-1.png: Setup: high plank with feet grounded, preparing to lean shoulders forward beyond wrists.
one-leg-planche-2.png: Near leg extends behind while far knee tucks under the torso; shoulders lean ahead of wrists.
one-leg-planche-3.png: Switch legs: near knee tucks under torso and far leg extends behind, maintaining forward shoulder lean.
straddle-planche-3.png: Full straddle planche hold with straight arms and shoulders ahead of wrists.
full-planche-1.png: Full hold: the body is one straight horizontal line from the head to the pointed toes, a hand-length above the floor, supported only on the hands. The arms are locked straight, the shoulders are protracted, the legs are together and straight and the hips are level.
planche-push-up-1.png: Full planche position facing right: the body in a straight horizontal line from the head to the pointed toes, the arms locked straight, the shoulders forward of the hands, the hands on the floor supporting the body with the feet off the floor.
planche-push-up-2.png: Lowering midway: the body stays in the horizontal straight line as the elbows bend to about 90 degrees and tuck beside the ribs. The torso descends toward the floor and the shoulders stay forward of the hands.
planche-push-up-3.png: Bottom position: the chest is just above the floor and the elbows bent past 90 degrees pressed into the ribs, the body is still a straight horizontal line with the feet off the floor and the shoulders ahead of the hands. Press back up to straight arms.
front-row-hold-1.png: Lying on the back under a low bar, facing up, hands gripping the bar overhand shoulder width, arms straight above the chest. The heels rest on the floor, the legs straight, the body in a straight line from the heels to the head, hanging.
front-row-hold-2.png: Pulling up: the elbows bend and travel back as the chest rises toward the bar. The body stays a rigid straight plank from the heels to the shoulders, the heels dig into the floor and the head stays in line with the spine.
front-row-hold-3.png: Full hold: the chest touching or just under the bar, elbows bent about 90 degrees tucked behind the ribs, shoulder blades pulled back and together. The body is a flat straight horizontal line from the heels to the head, feet supported on the floor and legs straight.
skin-the-cat-1.png: Hanging from the bar by an overhand shoulder-width grip with the arms straight. The hips pike up and the knees are tucked to the chest, the legs lifting toward the bar and the body beginning to curl backward.
skin-the-cat-2.png: Mid rotation: the body inverted beneath the bar, the hips above the head level with the bar and the legs passing between the arms. The shoulders are rotating behind the body and the arms are straight, the back arching slightly as the legs pass over.
skin-the-cat-3.png: Bottom: the legs lowered down behind in a German hang, the body hanging with the arms straight behind the back and the shoulders in full extension. The hips are below the bar, the back arched slightly, the feet pointing down toward the floor.
tuck-back-lever-1.png: Hanging from the bar with an overhand shoulder-width grip with the arms straight. The knees are tucked into the chest and the body is rolled backward into the inverted hang, the hips above the bar. The head is faceless and neutral, in line with the spine, with every limb position readable from this side (facing left) view of the Tuck Back Lever.
tuck-back-lever-2.png: Lowering back: the arms stay straight as the tucked body rotates down behind the bar into a face-down position, hips and knees tucked in, the shoulders moving into extension. Keep the faceless head neutral and aligned with the spine, and show every joint angle of the Tuck Back Lever clearly in this side (facing left) view.
tuck-back-lever-3.png: Full hold: the body faces the floor, the torso flat and horizontal, the arms straight and angled behind in line with the shoulders. The knees are tucked tight to the chest, hips bent, the head neutral with the neck in line with the torso and the shoulders in full extension.
advanced-tuck-back-lever-1.png: Hanging from the bar with an overhand shoulder-width grip with the arms straight. The knees are tucked in tight and the body is rotated backward, hips above the bar, inverted. The head is faceless and neutral, in line with the spine, with every limb position readable from this side (facing left) view of the Advanced Tuck Back Lever.
advanced-tuck-back-lever-2.png: Lowering to horizontal: the arms stay straight while the body rotates face down. The hips begin to open and the thighs move away from the chest while the shoulders are in extension. Keep the faceless head neutral and aligned with the spine, and show every joint angle of the Advanced Tuck Back Lever clearly in this side (facing left) view.
advanced-tuck-back-lever-3.png: Full hold: the torso is flat and horizontal facing the floor, the arms straight beneath the shoulders behind the bar. The hips are open so the thighs are in line with the back and the knees bent at about 90 degrees with the shins pointing down. The head is neutral.
advanced-tuck-front-lever-1.png: Hanging from the bar by an overhand shoulder-width grip, arms straight, shoulders packed. The knees are pulled tight to the chest in a tuck with the body hanging vertically beneath the bar, the head neutral. The head is faceless and neutral, in line with the spine, with every limb position readable from this side (facing right) view of the Advanced Tuck Front Lever.
advanced-tuck-front-lever-2.png: Rising: the straight arms stay vertical while the body rotates up toward horizontal. The hips open slowly, the thighs move away from the chest as the knees begin to extend backward while the back stays flat.
advanced-tuck-front-lever-3.png: Full hold: the torso is flat and horizontal with the arms straight and vertical. The hips are open so the thighs are in line with the back, the knees bent at 90 degrees with the shins pointing down. The knees are not tight to the chest, but the back stays flat, the shoulders pressed down.
crow-pose-1.png: Full hold: both feet off the floor, toes pointed and touching together behind the hips, shins resting on the backs of the upper arms. Arms straight or almost straight, back rounded and hips high, head lifted and looking ahead, shoulders forward of the wrists.
